title: Notable recent mathematics papers — arXiv announcement batch 2026-11-11
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred, and citation evidence is limited for these new papers.

sections.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
sections.abstract: For fixed integers k ≥ t ≥ 1 and ε > 0, the authors claim that every sufficiently high-degree k-uniform, t-simple multihypergraph H satisfies χ′(H) ≤ (t−1+1/t+ε)Δ(H).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract and Theorem 1.5 state a resolution of the Alon–Kim conjecture, open since 1997, across all fixed k,t; the paper identifies its finite-dimensional convex-optimization and probabilistic approach.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state that for each fixed k ≥ t ≥ 1 and ε > 0 there is a threshold Δ₀(k,t,ε) such that every k-uniform, t-simple multihypergraph with Δ(H) ≥ Δ₀ obeys the conjectured edge-colouring bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The hypergraph may have parallel edges; t-simplicity means distinct edges intersect in at most t vertices, and k,t,ε are fixed while Δ grows.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is asymptotic: the threshold depends on k,t,ε, and the paper does not make it a finite-degree sharp bound.

sections.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
sections.abstract: The author claims unconditionally that a positive proportion of consecutive nontrivial zeta-zero gaps are at most 0.7892 times their average spacing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a concrete unconditional improvement over the previously cited explicit threshold 1−2.36×10⁻⁶; its introduction states the theorem and the role of an unconditional variant of Montgomery’s pair-correlation method.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 states that D(λ) > 0 for every λ ≥ 0.7892, where D(λ) measures the lower limiting proportion of gaps no larger than λ times the mean spacing.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: This is an unconditional statement about the ordinates of nontrivial zeta zeros, counted with multiplicity; it concerns a positive proportion, not all gaps.
sections.unique_caveat: The author notes that the constant is not optimized; a different explicit kernel would give λ > 0.7864, and further optimization may improve it.

sections.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
sections.abstract: For the closure C_h of nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficient modulus at most h, the author claims connectedness exactly when h=q(q−1), q ≥ 2, and at least five components otherwise.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Theorem A supplies an if-and-only-if classification for every integer height; the paper also reports an explicit computational companion at Zenodo and connects the height-two case with a numerical observation from twenty years earlier.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that C_h is connected exactly at pronic heights and has at least five components at every other height, with further results showing infinitely many components for a density-one set of heights.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: C_h is the planar closure of nonreal roots of integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most the positive integer h; real roots are excluded before closure.
sections.unique_caveat: Exact component infinitude remains unsettled at a small set of heights, including 1, 3, 4, 9, and 25, and at some square-adjacent heights.

sections.title: The exponent 3/4 for the exceptional sets of the equations K/n=1/x+1/y+1/z
sections.abstract: For K ≥ 4, the author bounds the number E_K(N) of n ≤ N for which K/n has no representation as three positive unit fractions by N exp(−c((log N)³/K)^{1/4}) over a specified range, improving Vaughan’s exponent 2/3.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract and Theorem 1.1 report an improved uniform exceptional-set estimate, explicit constants, and a full Lean 4 formalization archived with the paper.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves E_K(N) ≤ N exp(−c((log N)³/K)^{1/4}) for absolute c>0 when 4 ≤ K ≤ (log N)³/B, with an explicit B; the proof is formally checked in Lean 4.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: E_K(N) counts integers 2 ≤ n ≤ N with no positive-integer solution to K/n=1/x+1/y+1/z; K=4 is the Erdős–Straus case, and the bound applies only in the stated K range and for sufficiently large N.
sections.unique_caveat: This improves a density bound but does not prove that every n is representable for K=4; its useful range is limited to K up to a constant multiple of (log N)³.

sections.title: A counterexample to the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture in dimensions three and higher
sections.abstract: For every n ≥ 3, r > 0, and ε > 0, the author constructs a compact set with the interior r-sphere condition but a point not covered by any contained ball of radius (1/2+ε)r, making the universal r/2 radius optimal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a dimension-by-dimension counterexample to the strong conjecture and an optimality conclusion for the universal radius, with an explicit simplex-based construction.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the strong conjecture fails in each dimension n ≥ 3, even for compact sets, and proves the universal contained-ball radius r/2 cannot be increased; in the plane the optimal radius is r/√3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The sets satisfy the interior r-sphere condition in Euclidean R^n; the counterexample is required for every positive ε and every n ≥ 3.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction establishes sharpness of the universal radius but does not classify all sets satisfying the sphere condition.

sections.title: Explicit restricted isometries with k=m^{2/3-o(1)}
sections.abstract: The authors construct explicit real m×n restricted isometries with m/n → 0, δ_k → 0, and sparsity k=m^{2/3-o(1)}, using a strongly regular graph and an incidence-geometric vertex-set result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a concrete explicit construction cross-listed across functional analysis, information theory, combinatorics, and metric geometry; the authors frame it as surpassing an m^{1/2} barrier for the stated entrywise-Gram-matrix proof technique.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove existence of the stated family and show that the barrier for their proof method is m^{2/3}, which their construction reaches up to the o(1) in the exponent.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The matrices are real; m tends to infinity, the aspect ratio m/n tends to zero, and the restricted isometry constant δ_k tends to zero.
sections.unique_caveat: The exponent is 2/3−o(1), not an exact k=m^{2/3} guarantee; the paper’s result is an explicit family under these asymptotic conditions.

sections.title: Progression-free sets in class 2 and arbitrary finite groups
sections.abstract: The author transfers bounds through nilpotent groups of class 2 to prove r₃(G) ≤ C|G| exp(−c(log|G|)^{1/6}/(log log|G|)^{1/3}) for every sufficiently large finite group G.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives an explicit asymptotic form for arbitrary finite groups and identifies a transfer of sharp abelian bounds via class-2 nilpotent groups as the proof route; it cross-lists group theory and number theory.
sections.claimed_result: Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author’s theorem on large class-2 subgroups yields the stated upper bound, improving estimates based on Pyber’s abelian-subgroup theorem.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: G ranges over arbitrary finite groups as |G|→∞; r₃(G) denotes the maximum size of a three-term-progression-free subset in the paper’s group setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is asymptotic and the abstract does not specify numerical values for its constants C and c.

sections.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
sections.abstract: The author rules out a 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus, a case left open by standard lower bounds for the conjectured 15-vertex minimum.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract isolates a specific gap in a vertex-minimality conjecture and reports a proof combining a g₂ inequality, a simplicial-complement reduction, fundamental groups, and Alexander duality.
sections.claimed_result: The author excludes the 13-vertex case by reducing to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus and deriving a contradiction from the deficiency of Z³.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The object is a simplicial triangulation of the three-torus; the result addresses exactly 13 vertices.
sections.unique_caveat: The 14-vertex case remains undecided by this paper, so it does not establish the conjectured 15-vertex minimum.

sections.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
sections.abstract: For H_d: y²=φ_d(x), the authors classify pairs (d,p), with p prime not dividing 2d, for which H_d is maximal over a finite field of characteristic p and determine the corresponding fields.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims a complete classification in a defined family, including the previously partial p≡1 mod 4 case, and a Frobenius-polynomial computation for the stated odd-degree subcase.
sections.claimed_result: For odd d and p≡1 mod 4, the authors state that the Jacobian is supersingular exactly when H_d becomes maximal over a finite extension, and this occurs precisely for d=ℓ^n with prime ℓ≡1 mod 4 and p a generator modulo ℓ^n; they also compute the Frobenius polynomial.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The curves are the Chebyshev family y²=φ_d(x); p is prime with p∤2d, and the detailed equivalence quoted applies to odd d and p≡1 mod 4.
sections.unique_caveat: This classification concerns the specified Chebyshev-derived family, not arbitrary hyperelliptic curves.

sections.title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
sections.abstract: The author gives counterexamples to unimodality and log-concavity claims in a rank-two annular cluster model, proves a skew-shape block-statistic identity under a specified convention, and provides Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports two concrete counterexamples, a positive identity result, and an available complete Lean formalization; the paper is a self-contained combinatorial contribution with a checkable proof artifact.
sections.claimed_result: The author refutes a published unimodality assertion and a log-concavity conjecture in the rank-two annular model, while proving a skew-Young-diagram block-statistic identity proposed in earlier work.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The counterexamples use the stated annular cluster model; the identity holds for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams under the paper’s explicit root-exclusion convention.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexamples depend on the model and conventions specified in the paper; they do not establish failure of unimodality or log-concavity beyond that setting.
